name: obs-web
description: OBS-web - the easiest way to control OBS remotely
readme_summary: OBS-web is a browser-based application that allows users to remotely control OBS Studio, offering features like scene switching, stream/recording control, and live preview. It requires OBS version 28+ and the obs-websocket plugin, and can be accessed locally or over the internet via WSS tunnels.
key_features: Support for local network and internet control (WSS tunnels)
Switch scenes, start/stop streaming and recording
Live preview of program & preview scenes
Hide/switch sources with specific naming conventions
primary_use_case: Remotely controlling OBS Studio from a web browser on any device.
cover_image_prompt: A conductor standing at a futuristic podium, orchestrating a complex live broadcast. The conductor's hands gesture, and in response, different scenes (represented by glowing holographic panels) seamlessly transition on a large screen behind them. One panel shows a live camera feed, another a graphic, and another a gameplay scene. Subtle digital streams of data flow from the podium to the screen, and the OBS-web logo is visible on the conductor's tablet. The scene is set in a modern, dimly lit control room with a vibrant, energetic atmosphere. The style is a 3D isometric illustration with clean lines and glowing accents, emphasizing control and ease of use.

name: friday-showcase
description: Friday — A 24/7 AI Assistant Built Entirely on Claude Code
readme_summary: Friday is a 24/7 AI assistant that runs entirely on Claude Code CLI, leveraging its built-in capabilities for tool use, scheduling, and memory. It aims to provide a self-evolving AI system without custom AI backends, cloud VMs, or fine-tuning, making it accessible on standard machines.
key_features: Built Entirely on Claude Code CLI
No custom AI, cloud VMs, or fine-tuning
Runs on standard Windows, Linux, or macOS
Self-evolving capabilities (skills, reflection, preference learning, proposals)
primary_use_case: To create a continuously running, self-improving personal AI assistant that can manage tasks, learn from interactions, and evolve its capabilities using only the Claude Code CLI and its integrated tools.
cover_image_prompt: A wise, old owl perched on a stack of books, with a glowing digital network emanating from its eyes, connecting to various tools like a calendar, a file cabinet, and a Telegram chat bubble. The owl is actively 'reading' the books (representing Claude Code's system prompt and knowledge) and 'speaking' through the chat bubble, while also managing the other tools with subtle gestures. Small, ethereal streams of data flow from the tools towards the owl, symbolizing learning and memory. The background is a softly lit, organized study. The overall style is a 3D isometric illustration with a warm, inviting color palette, emphasizing intelligence and continuous operation.

name: ytsurf
description: YouTube in your terminal. Clean and distraction-free.
readme_summary: ytsurf is a command-line tool that allows users to watch and download YouTube videos directly from their terminal. It offers a clean, distraction-free interface and integrates with various terminal-based menu selectors for an interactive experience.
key_features: Integration with fzf, rofi, sentaku, and tv for menu selection
primary_use_case: Watching and downloading YouTube content within a terminal environment with a focus on a clean and interactive user experience.
cover_image_prompt: A minimalist, stylized terminal window is open, displaying a vibrant, flowing stream of YouTube video thumbnails. A single, glowing cursor hovers over one thumbnail, indicating selection. Subtle digital particles emanate from the terminal, suggesting data transfer. In the background, a faint, abstract representation of a globe hints at the internet source. The repository name 'ytsurf' is subtly integrated into the terminal's status bar. The overall mood is clean and focused, with a cool, digital color palette. The style should be a 3D isometric illustration with a focus on clean lines and glowing elements.

name: RepoRewind
readme_summary: RepoRewind is a developer tool that visualizes Git history in interactive 3D using WebGL and provides AI-powered narrative summaries of codebase evolution. It offers a zero-configuration experience, transforming complex commit logs into an engaging visual timeline.
key_features: Interactive 3D Architecture Graph with physics engine and folder collapsing
4D Time Scrubbing to navigate repository history
Local AI Storyteller (WebLLM) for narrative summaries
Dynamic physics for smooth branch animations
Visual hierarchy with distinct node types (root, directories, files)
primary_use_case: Visualizing and understanding the evolution of a codebase over time through an interactive 3D graph and AI-generated historical narratives.
cover_image_prompt: A whimsical, glowing 3D tree of life representing a software project's history. The roots are deep, dark, and complex, symbolizing the initial commits. As the branches grow upwards, they become brighter and more structured, with leaves and fruits representing features and stable versions. Small, ethereal figures (developers) are seen tending to the tree, pruning branches (refactoring) or planting new seeds (new features). Subtle digital particles flow along the branches, indicating data and dependencies. The repository name 'RepoRewind' is subtly etched into the trunk. The overall mood is one of growth, discovery, and clarity in complexity. Style: 3D isometric illustration with a dark, magical, and futuristic aesthetic, vibrant glowing elements, and clean, readable details.

name: clover-helper
readme_summary: Clover Helper is a VS Code extension designed for Russian-speaking developers. It automatically translates code comments into Russian and provides quick access to documentation and tutorials for selected code snippets directly within VS Code's integrated browser.
key_features: Translate comments in the current file or entire project
Search for code documentation in Russian using an integrated browser
Search for beginner-friendly video tutorials on YouTube in Russian
Translate docstrings in hover tooltips with caching
primary_use_case: To enhance the coding experience for Russian-speaking developers by localizing code comments and facilitating easier access to relevant documentation and learning resources.
cover_image_prompt: A friendly, wise owl wearing a small VS Code cap, perched on a stack of code books. The owl is holding a magnifying glass over a line of English code, and a speech bubble above it shows the same code translated into Russian. To the side, a small, open browser window displays a Russian documentation page related to the code. Subtle digital particles flow from the code to the translation and the browser, symbolizing the seamless integration. The background is a soft, gradient blue, evoking a calm and productive coding environment. The overall style is a charming 3D isometric illustration, emphasizing clarity and helpfulness.

name: vpn-configurator
readme_summary: This is a client-only web application built with TypeScript and Vite that helps users configure AllowedIPs for AmneziaWG/WireGuard VPNs. It allows users to select inclusion/exclusion strategies, integrate system service lists, and add manual CIDRs to generate a single, clean line of configuration for their VPN peer settings, all stored locally in the browser.
key_features: Include / exclude strategies with CIDR merge and subtract (IPv4 + IPv6)
System IP lists (YouTube, ChatGPT, Discord, Telegram, …) as locked URL entries
primary_use_case: Configuring WireGuard AllowedIPs for split tunneling using AmneziaWG.
cover_image_prompt: A digital cartographer meticulously drawing a complex network map on a large, glowing parchment. The map is divided into distinct regions, some highlighted in vibrant colors (representing included services) and others marked with exclusion zones. Small, stylized icons of popular online services like YouTube and Discord are subtly integrated into the map. In the foreground, a clean, single line of code or a simplified IP address range is being precisely etched onto the map, ready to be copied. The overall mood is one of organized precision and digital creation, with subtle UI elements and data particles floating around the scene. The art style is a 3D isometric illustration with a clean, modern aesthetic and a focus on clear visual representation of data routing.
